subject: Exec sign-off: transition buffer & downscale protection for Meridian Health pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@meridianhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-18T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: early exit carve-out + transition buffer for pilot

Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Before we finalize the pilot PO, Procurement has one ask we need Redwood's guidance on: we need an early-exit carve-out that lets us wind down the pilot after month 3 with a short transition buffer and protections for downscaling so our internal security/ops teams can decommission safely.

High level:
- Pilot term: 6 months, but Meridian is requesting an option to terminate after month 3 with 30 days' notice and a 60-day transition buffer where Redwood maintains reserved capacity and preserves model cache for our prefix keys (to avoid re-warm cost).
- Financials: Meridian is willing to accept a 40% prorated refund/credit for committed capacity if we both agree on a staged ramp-down schedule.
- Legal wants explicit opt-in language for the staged ramp (we will choose whether to activate the opt-in within the first 45 days).

Attaching Procurement's redline of the amendment (PDF) and a proposed ramp schedule CSV for your reference. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these elements and, if not, what concessions you can offer?

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Meridian Health
attachments: Meridian_Amendment_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf), ramp_schedule_table.csv (csv)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-19T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: early exit carve-out + transition buffer for pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and for sending the redline. I reviewed with the Deal Desk and wanted to get ahead of expectations while we pull Legal into the loop. Quick summary of what we can support and open questions: 

What Redwood can support (prelim):
- 30 days' formal notice to terminate followed by a 60-day transition buffer where we hold reserved capacity and prioritize your traffic on the same model variant.
- During the 60-day buffer we can preserve key components of prefix/KV cache for up to 45 days post-notice; longer cache retention is operationally expensive and we would need a specific paid retention add-on.
- Staged ramp opt-in: acceptable, but we need a binding schedule table and a cap on total reserved GPU-hours during the buffer period (we've attached our preferred ramp table in the attached CSV).

Open items for exec/legal approval:
- Financial unwind: Meridian proposes a 40% prorated refund/credit for committed capacity on early exit. This is outside standard termination language and needs Deal Desk/Finance sign-off (this is the main escalation).
- Whether we put a hard cap on cache preservation costs or treat it as an add-on with an explicit cost card.

I am looping in Marissa (Deal Desk) and Karthik (Sales Ops) to request an executive sign-off (or escalation to Finance) on the 40% credit and the cache-retention concession. If approved, Legal will draft final amendment language and we'll push DocuSign.

Next steps I propose:
1) Exec approval on the 40% prorated credit (or alternate %).
2) Decide whether cache retention is included in the pilot at no charge, or listed as a chargeable add-on.
3) Finalize ramp schedule and opt-in language, then route to Legal.

Lukas Meyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-11-20T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Exec approval request: Meridian Health — early termination & transition buffer (DEAL-2027-0458)

Team — forwarding Meridian's request (below) and our summary. Need a quick decision on the early-exit credit and cache-retention handling so I can reply to Procurement and keep timeline for PO.

Background: Meridian is a strategic healthcare POC. They want an opt-in for a staged ramp and an early exit after month 3 with 30 days' notice plus a 60-day transition buffer. They propose a 40% prorated credit for committed capacity on early termination.

My recommendation:
- Approve a 25% prorated credit (compromise) rather than 40%.
- Include 45 days of free prefix/KV cache preservation during the 60-day buffer; beyond that, charge a flat retention fee ($X per reserved GPU-day).
- Require Meridian to sign the attached ramp schedule CSV within 10 business days to enable the opt-in — otherwise the opt-in window closes.

Rationale: 25% preserves most of the business economics while giving Meridian flexibility. Free cache retention for 45 days keeps re-warm costs reasonable; beyond that, we avoid operational surprise. Requiring the signed schedule eliminates open-ended ambiguity.

Ask: Please respond with APPROVE / REJECT / MODIFY and any edits to the numbers above. If APPROVE, confirm whether Deal Desk wants Legal to accept the 25% credit as-is or add an explicit cap on cumulative credits across product lines.

Full Meridian request copied below for context. Attachments: Meridian_Amendment_Draft_v3.pdf, ramp_schedule_table.csv

Regards,
Lukas

Subject: Re: Exec approval request: Meridian Health — early termination & transition buffer (DEAL-2027-0458)

Lukas — thanks for the clear framing and recommendation. After reviewing with Finance and Legal we can APPROVE with the following conditions: 

1) Credit: Approve a 30% prorated credit on committed capacity for early termination (compromise between 25% and 40%). Cap cumulative credits tied to this pilot to the committed spend under DEAL-2027-0458 only (no cross-product aggregation).

2) Transition buffer & cache retention: Agree to the 60-day buffer, and include 45 days of free prefix/KV cache preservation. After 45 days, cache preservation will be charged per the retention add-on schedule (attach cost card in Legal's amendment).

3) Ramp opt-in: Meridian must return the signed ramp_schedule_table.csv within 10 business days of this approval to preserve opt-in rights. If they miss the window, opt-in is void.

4) Documentation: Legal to incorporate explicit language that the transition buffer is not a capacity guarantee beyond reserved GPU-hours listed in the ramp CSV; Redwood reserves the right to reallocate excess capacity if billed hours are not honored.

5) Executed amendment required: This approval is conditional on Legal executing the amendment and DocuSign completion. No credit will be applied without a fully executed amendment.

Please proceed to Legal with these terms and copy Finance for tracking. Lukas — reply to Jordan with the approved numbers and next steps; copy Legal (legal@redwoodinference.com) and include the amended cost card.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
